observations.title: Akan volcano (Japan)
observations.description: The Japan Meteorological Agency (JMA) reported that no eruptions at Akan (also known as Meakan-dake, which means Meakan Peak) of the Akan volcanic complex were recorded after 15 March; unrest continued to decline. Sulfur dioxide emissions averaged 300-400 tons per day (t/d) during February-April but declined to 100-200 t/d starting in June. Steam-and-gas emissions also became less dense and vigorous. Seismicity began to decrease in June and was characterized as low in October. The Alert Level was lowered to 1 (the lowest level on a 5-level scale) at 1000 on 4 November. Source: Japan Meteorological Agency (JMA)
